chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Harry Carney as a boyhood friend
summary: Holmes describes Carney's birth, family, strict upbringing and gentlemanly character; they shared school and Dr. Holmes's band but did not socialize.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What I want to do now is to discuss your friendship with Harry Carney.

Harry Carney. Born April First -- no fool -- 1910. I guess he was born in Boston; that's where I met him. I don't know exactly where he was born. He had a brother named Wendell Carney, a beautiful mother and a beautiful daddy. As far as I know of them. He was brought up very strict by his mother.
He was a classmate of yours, too, wasn't he?

Yes. We were classmates for many years. Until we finished grammar school, we were classmates. And then he went to English High School and I went to Mechanical Arts High School. But we were always friends, and we lived in the same neighborhood.
You also then went with Dr. Holmes's band?
That's right. We both went in that band together. We applied for instruments together. And he got

a clarinet and I got an oboe.
Harry was a very... He was very ambitious, and he liked to study. And he was very nervy. He had plenty of drive, you know. Make himself known wherever he went. He was very a well-mannered person, very congenial. And he was a real gentleman, all down through his career as a musician. All I can say about him, he was a real gentleman. He loved people and he knew how to talk and associate with people.
You and Harry, would you go to dances together?

No-no-no. We didn't socialize together. Only as a bunch of kids would do, a bunch of boys. Because he had certain chores to do at home. His mother raised him pretty close, you know. Which was good. Ain't nothin' wrong with that. But a lot of times I was allowed to be in the streets, and he wasn't, because he had to do chores and this, that and the other. But he was very well brought up, and he was always a gentleman. That's all I can say.
